tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Kits
tips.text: To remove old paint without damaging kit parts, use a mixture of water and dish soap. Soak the parts in the solution for 10-15 minutes, then gently scrub with an old toothbrush. For stubborn paint, use a cotton swab dipped in rubbing alcohol. After cleaning, rinse with water and allow to dry completely before painting.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: To repair broken photo-etch parts, use CA (Cyanoacrylate) glue. Apply a small amount on the inside of the break, pressing the pieces together tightly. Let it dry for 5 minutes, then apply a small amount on the outside and clamp the pieces together. Once dry, use a file or sandpaper to remove excess glue and smooth the joint.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To unclog an airbrush, first disassemble it according to the manufacturer's instructions. Soak the nozzle and needle in Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for 15 minutes, then scrub gently with a toothbrush. Reassemble the airbrush, and test it with fresh thinner to ensure it's clear. If still clogged, use an Iwata airbrush cleaning kit.

tips.title: Repairing Warped Parts
tips.text: To fix warped parts, use a combination of heat and pressure. Place the warped part on a flat surface, then lay a piece of glass on top. Use a heat gun to gently heat the glass (not the part directly), then use weights or clamps to apply even pressure. Allow it to cool completely before removing the weights.

tips.title: Avoiding Frost from Rattle Cans
tips.text: To prevent frost from forming when using rattle cans in cold conditions, warm the can in warm water (not hot) for 5-10 minutes before use. Shake the can vigorously for at least 2 minutes to ensure the paint is well mixed. Test spray on a scrap surface before painting the model. Always store cans upright to prevent paint from settling.
